history.heading: Arabia and the birth of Islam
paragraphs: The Arabian Peninsula was home to ancient trading kingdoms; the Nabataean city of Hegra (Al-Ula) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Mecca was a trading and religious centre. Around 610 CE the Prophet Muhammad began preaching Islam in Mecca. After the migration (Hijra) to Medina in 622, Islam spread across Arabia, and within a century Arab caliphates ruled from Spain to Central Asia.

After the capital of the caliphate moved away, the Hejaz, with Mecca and Medina, came under the rule of local sharifs and later the Ottoman Empire, while central Arabia (Najd) was divided among tribes.

history.heading: The Saudi states
paragraphs: In 1744 Muhammad bin Saud allied with the religious reformer Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, founding the first Saudi state, which was destroyed by Ottoman-Egyptian forces in 1818. A second Saudi state followed.

In 1902 Abdulaziz ibn Saud recaptured Riyadh and, over three decades, conquered most of the peninsula, including the Hejaz in 1925. He proclaimed the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in 1932. Oil was discovered in 1938.

history.heading: The oil kingdom
paragraphs: Oil wealth transformed Saudi Arabia from a poor desert kingdom into one of the richest countries in the world. In 1979 militants seized the Grand Mosque in Mecca, after which religious conservatism increased. Saudi Arabia hosted US forces during the 1991 Gulf War. Fifteen of the 19 hijackers in the 2001 September 11 attacks were Saudi.

Since 2017, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has led rapid social and economic changes, including allowing women to drive and opening entertainment, while cracking down on dissent; the 2018 murder of journalist Jamal Khashoggi drew global condemnation.

culture.heading: Faith and society
paragraphs: Arabic is the official language. Islam is the state religion, and Saudi Arabia is home to the two holiest sites of Islam, the Great Mosque in Mecca and the Prophet's Mosque in Medina, receiving millions of pilgrims for the Hajj and Umrah. Most citizens are Sunni, with a Shia minority in the east. About 40 percent of residents are foreign workers.
Traditional culture includes Arabic poetry, falconry, the ardah sword dance and coffee with dates. Kabsa (spiced rice with meat) is the national dish.

culture.heading: Changing society
paragraphs: Under Vision 2030, cinemas, concerts and tourist visas were introduced, and restrictions on women have been relaxed. Saudi Arabia has invested heavily in sports, buying football clubs and stars, hosting major events and winning the right to host the 2034 FIFA World Cup.

politics.heading: Absolute monarchy
paragraphs: Saudi Arabia is an absolute monarchy ruled by the Al Saud family. The king, currently King Salman, holds supreme authority, and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, also prime minister, runs the government in practice. There is no elected parliament, and political parties are banned. Human rights groups criticise the use of the death penalty and the imprisonment of critics.
Saudi Arabia is a leading power in the Arab and Muslim world and has led a military intervention in Yemen since 2015. It restored relations with Iran in 2023.

economy.heading: Oil and Vision 2030
paragraphs: Saudi Arabia has one of the largest oil reserves in the world and is a leading producer and exporter. Saudi Aramco is one of the world's most valuable companies. Saudi Arabia leads OPEC+ in managing oil supply.

Vision 2030 aims to diversify the economy through tourism, entertainment, mining, manufacturing and technology, with giant projects such as NEOM. The Public Investment Fund is one of the largest sovereign wealth funds. The riyal is pegged to the US dollar.
